summary:
ECHOES transforms the legacy of space exploration into an adventure of scientific discovery. We developed an educational game in which players become astronauts and investigate historic equipment left on the Moon and Mars, including the Eagle lunar module, ALSEP experiments, the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, and the Ingenuity helicopter.

Through interactive exploration, the project connects students with the stories and scientific contributions of this equipment. Each discovery reveals an object’s mission, purpose, and scientific significance, drawing on official NASA sources. After completing both levels, players receive a discovery report that brings together what they learned throughout their journey.

Built with JavaScript and Phaser 3, the working prototype already delivers this complete experience and can accommodate additional equipment and missions. Planned development includes pilot projects in schools and science centers to evaluate learning and guide improvements.

By turning the legacy of space missions into a participatory experience, ECHOES aims to spark curiosity, encourage investigation, and connect future generations with the science that made space exploration possible.
details:
What can humanity learn from the equipment it has left behind on other worlds? This question guides ECHOES, an educational 2D space exploration game developed by the Cangaceiros Estelares team. Created for the “Abandoned but Not Forgotten” challenge, the project transforms the stories of equipment left on the Moon and Mars into an interactive experience of investigation, discovery, and learning.

In ECHOES, players control an astronaut and explore two environments: first the Moon, and then Mars. Movement is controlled using the arrow keys or WASD. When approaching a piece of equipment, players can investigate it by pressing E. This interaction displays an information panel containing details about the mission, the equipment's purpose, its scientific contribution, and the source used. These discoveries guide the player's progress and are compiled into a final report, allowing players to revisit the information gathered throughout their journey.

The prototype features five pieces of equipment organized into four investigation groups: the descent stage of the Eagle lunar module; the ALSEP scientific experiments; the Spirit and Opportunity rovers, presented together; and the Ingenuity helicopter. The content was structured using records from the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA) and official NASA Science webpages. These references connect the gameplay experience to the scientific and historical information that supports it.

Our creative approach lies in transforming historical equipment into discovery points within an adventure. Players encounter objects in the environment, investigate their stories, and build a record of their exploration. The pixel art visual identity brings the content closer to the language of video games, while the stylized environments help create an atmosphere of curiosity. The astronaut's journey is an educational narrative that brings together equipment from different missions in a single experience.

The game was developed using JavaScript for programming and Phaser 3 as the 2D game framework, incorporating features such as scenes, animations, camera controls, interaction, and movement through Arcade Physics. HTML and CSS structure and present the webpage that hosts the game. Vite, Node.js, and npm support the development environment, dependency management, and generation of the web version. We used Figma for interface planning and OpenAI AI tools to support the creation of illustrations and visual materials. The project was designed to run in a desktop web browser using a keyboard, without requiring specialized hardware.

Throughout development, we prioritized accuracy in relation to scientific sources, clarity of information, simple controls, the connection between exploration and reading, and the possibility of expanding the content. We also defined a scope that would allow us to deliver a complete journey during the hackathon. The code organization into scenes, entities, and equipment data provides a foundation for incorporating new missions and discoveries.

The intended benefit is to offer an engaging introduction to the history and science of space exploration. For students, the game aims to spark questions and encourage investigation. For teachers and science centers, it can serve as a starting point for activities and discussions about technology, space missions, and the development of scientific knowledge.

We already have a functional prototype featuring both levels, equipment investigations, and a discovery report. The proposed next step is to conduct a pilot with students, supported by educational guidance, observing their understanding of the controls and their ability to explain the purpose and contributions of the equipment. This evaluation will guide improvements and help assess the educational outcomes.

With ECHOES, we want every piece of equipment players encounter to inspire a new question, and every discovery to bring them closer to the people, technologies, and science behind these missions. Every mission leaves a story — and these stories can inspire the next generation of explorers.
